summary.title: Minimum Viable Security - Wharton Web Conference 2015
summary.one_liner: A talk outlining five simple steps a startup or small team can take to build a starter security program that grows with the product.
keywords: security without a dedicated security engineer
takeaways: Startups and small business units often lack a dedicated security team, so security must be bootstrapped.
The talk proposes five simple steps to create a minimum viable security program.
A minimum viable security program starts small and is iterated on as the product and business grow.
summary.summary: This is the speaker deck page for a talk given at the Wharton Web Conference in July 2015. The talk argues that lean startups and small business units can still have security, even without a large security organization or even a single dedicated security engineer. It presents five simple steps for creating a "minimum viable security program" that can be expanded over time. The page text is only the talk description, so the specific steps are not listed here.
